gen-dafont-good-times-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum is a dignified text serif with a high, squared-off x-height and a c that gapes wide. Suwannaphum holds the page together while Good Times, with its geometric, commanding heft, supplies the shout.
gen-dafont-good-times-manrope:
Manrope reads friendly and bright, its curves left open.

Good Times lays down wide, geometric, commanding headings with a moderate shift in stroke, and the sans below follows with one steady line, minimal fuss and a gentle step from capitals to lowercase.
gen-dafont-good-times-montserrat: Montserrat glides along with generous white space at every curve and oversized counters in its e and a. And Good Times adds a heavier, commanding geometric voice, so the two feel related yet clearly different in weight.
gen-dafont-good-times-satoshi:
Satoshi stands tall and wide-open, cut in one wire-like line.

Good Times is best at geometric, commanding display shapes with a close stem-to-hairline ratio, whereas Satoshi's strength is a soaring x-height and a sans-serif skeleton that never looks squeezed.
gen-dafont-good-times-switzer:
Thick, cable-like lowercase gives Good Times its commanding presence.

It earns its keep when the words are big and brief, while Switzer, a Swiss-flavored sans-serif with tubular letterforms and a tall waist line, stays friendly beside it.
gen-dafont-groovy-bitter:
Bitter looks dependable and grounded, with a big lowercase eye.

Read at length, its slab-serif letters stay open and easy to see through, a clear contrast to the almost-shut c of the funky Groovy heading.
gen-dafont-groovy-fs-bespoke-sans: Friendly and funky, Groovy loosens its lowercase and pinches its c nearly shut. Bespoke Sans answers with sharp, refined sans-serif letters, curves ending well away from the stem, so tight meets open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab reads classic and dignified, its c gaping visibly and its lowercase tall and rounded. Groovy is best at friendly, funky, tightly closed headline shapes, but the body letters are best at staying open and steady.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-fauna-one:
Fauna One reads literary and dignified, with a tall middle band.

Groovy's thick-and-thin-free arms and legs bring a funky, friendly lift above that quiet serif, whose low contrast and open e keep the lines calm.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-kadwa:
Kadwa reads classic and editorial, its open-ended curves and larger-than-usual x-height keeping each line easy to follow, unlike Groovy's near-closed c.

A longer stretch stays smooth and low in contrast.
